name: Taranto
title: Taranto Ship Thickness Gauging | UTM for Bulkers & Tankers
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Taranto for ore and coal bulkers, refinery tankers and container ships: hold, ballast tank, deck and piping gauging.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships at the Port of Taranto
intro: Taranto is a steel, naval and container port on the Gulf of Taranto, and its ships run from ore and coal carriers for the steelworks to refinery tankers and container feeders. A ship is gauged here to keep its steel record current before a survey, to close out items left from the last one, or to give a buyer or a repair yard firm numbers. Our technicians travel from India to the vessel for each job; nobody is stationed in Puglia, so scope and permits are settled before anyone flies.

highlights.h: Steelworks bulkers with worn hold steel
highlights.p: Ore and coal carriers serving the steel plant leave hold frames, lower side shell and tank top scarred by abrasive cargo, so hold gauging after discharge is the core Taranto job and often decides how much steel a later yard stay must renew.

highlights.h: Refinery jetties and a container terminal
highlights.p: Product tankers at the refinery berths and container ships at the Yilport terminal add deck, piping and scrubber-line work, so one mobilisation can cover very different ship types within the same Ionian port.

highlights.h: Open Ionian approach, little tidal delay
highlights.p: The deep outer bay and the small tidal range mean ships berth and sail close to schedule, which helps a gauging team plan a working day alongside without waiting on water level.

port.h: The port of Taranto: Mar Grande, the steel quays and the Mar Piccolo
p: Taranto lies on the northern shore of the Gulf of Taranto, in the instep of the Italian boot. Ships enter the Mar Grande, an outer bay sheltered by breakwaters and the Cheradi islands, and the commercial quays and industrial jetties sit along its northern and eastern shores. Behind them lies the Mar Piccolo, an inner sea reached through a dredged channel beneath a swing bridge, much of it used by the navy. The approach from the Ionian is deep and open and the tidal range is small, so water level seldom holds a ship back. Winter gales from the south and west can stop pilots and tugs for a while and unsettle ships waiting outside the breakwater.

Bulk cargo for the steelworks shapes the port more than anything else. Ore and coal carriers discharge at the plant's own quays, and steel products leave again as coils and plate on general cargo ships. Tankers call at the refinery jetties with crude or deliver and load refined products. The container terminal, run by Yilport, receives feeder and some larger container ships on transhipment and Mediterranean services, and the multipurpose quays handle project cargo such as wind-energy components, cement and other bulk goods. The navy base occupies much of the Mar Piccolo and has its own separate ship movements.

For anyone planning thickness gauging, the mix matters. Bulk carriers that carry abrasive raw materials need hold, tank top and lower hopper readings far more often than a ship in clean trades. The volume of ore and coal follows the output of the steelworks, which has changed sharply in recent years, so calls by dry bulkers are less regular than at a pure commodity port. A ship in the Gulf waiting for a berth may lie at anchor for days, which sometimes turns an idle period into a window for an owner's condition check.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Taranto: industrial quays, jetties and the Gulf
p: Almost every Taranto job is done alongside at an industrial or terminal berth. The steelworks quays work to their own rules on dust, hot work and cargo handling, so the agent arranges access and a safety induction first, and holds can be entered only once discharge is complete and the stevedores have left the space. Residual ore dust and moisture on frames and tank tops make surface preparation part of the plan: readings on coated or scaled steel are only as good as the cleaning behind them, and we agree with the ship's crew who prepares which locations before the team arrives.

Docking is not a strong point of the port for commercial ships. The naval arsenal in the Mar Piccolo is a military facility and is not where merchant ships are normally gauged or repaired, so owners with a ship loading at Taranto generally book their drydock at a yard elsewhere in Italy, in Greece, in Malta or on the Croatian coast. A thickness survey alongside in Taranto, carried out before the ship sails, lets the chosen yard plan steel renewal from measured figures instead of assumptions, and the same readings then serve as the baseline against which the yard's own gauging is compared.
list: Steelworks quays — hold frames, tank top and lower hopper plating on ore and coal carriers once discharge is complete and the holds are cleared
Refinery jetties — main deck, deck piping and accessible ballast tanks on product tankers, under the terminal's strict ignition-source rules
Container terminal quays — hatch covers, cross-deck structure and scrubber overboard piping on feeder and larger container ships during cargo work
Multipurpose and project cargo quays — gauging of general cargo ships and heavy-lift vessels between loading windows
Anchorage in the Gulf of Taranto — owner's condition gauging on ships waiting for a berth or laid up, reached by a launch the agent books

context.h: Port state control, regulation and the steel trade in Taranto
p: Ships calling at Taranto are boarded for port state control by the Italian Coast Guard, working through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto) under the Paris MoU. Targeting follows the ship risk profile, so an older bulk carrier with a poor inspection history is likelier to be boarded, and structural deficiencies such as wasted hold frames or holed tank tops are among the findings that can lead to detention. Bulk carriers fall under the ESP regime from their first renewal survey, and the extensive gauging required at the later special surveys makes a prior measured baseline valuable. Older ships in the ore and coal trades often reach this point with real wastage in the holds.

Wider rules add reasons to know the steel state of a ship. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires ships calling at EU ports to carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and a ship nearing the end of its commercial life will be assessed for sale or recycling against its gauging record. EU ETS now covers shipping emissions and FuelEU Maritime applies to fuel use, which bears on the economics of keeping older handysize and panamax bulkers in service. Finally, the steel plant's own supply chain is exposed to freight and charter terms, so charterers acting for the mills tend to ask about structural condition before accepting tonnage.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Taranto
jobs.p: Taranto requests cluster around bulk carriers after discharge and tankers at the refinery berths. A bulker may be alongside for a few days while cargo is worked, which gives a team time for cleaned holds and tank tops, and a tanker at a jetty offers deck and piping access. The superintendent and the team agree the list of spaces, permits and the report layout in advance, so the readings are ready to put in front of a class surveyor, a charterer or a prospective buyer.
list: Hold frame, lower side shell and tank top gauging on an ore carrier at the steelworks quay, after discharge and cleaning, ahead of a renewal survey
Pre-docking gauging of a coal carrier's topside and hopper tanks so a yard in the Mediterranean can plan steel renewal before the ship arrives
Main deck and deck piping gauging on a product tanker at a refinery jetty, with the ballast tanks the ship declares safe for entry
Hatch cover and coaming readings on a container feeder during cargo work, plus a wall-thickness check of the scrubber overboard line
Owner's condition gauging on a general cargo ship at anchor in the Gulf of Taranto before an on-hire or sale decision

logistics: Taranto-Grottaglie Airport is the nearest airport but has limited services, so teams usually fly into Bari or Brindisi and continue by road. Port access for the steelworks quays, refinery jetties and container terminal is arranged by the ship's agent, with ISPS passes and any terminal induction booked ahead. Our technicians are Indian nationals and travel on Schengen visas, whose lead time depends on the consulate, so we begin the application as soon as the call is firm and fix flights once the ship's berth date is confirmed.
vessels: Container feeders and larger container ships

faqs.q: Can holds on an ore carrier be gauged at the steelworks quay?
faqs.a: Yes, once the cargo is out and the stevedores have cleared the hold. Dust and moisture on frames and tank tops affect the readings, so the crew or a cleaning gang prepares the locations beforehand. We agree which spaces are cleaned, mark the measurement points on the drawings, and record the condition of the surface alongside every reading.

faqs.q: Is there a commercial drydock in Taranto for a renewal survey?
faqs.a: Not for ordinary merchant ships on a regular basis. The naval arsenal serves the navy, so owners normally book a yard in Greece, Malta, Croatia or elsewhere in Italy. We gauge the ship in Taranto first so the yard has measured steel estimates, then mobilise a team to the yard for the full programme if you ask.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at anchor in the Gulf of Taranto?
faqs.a: Yes, for suitable spaces and in suitable weather. A launch booked by the agent takes the team out, and gauging is limited to spaces that are safe to enter and reachable without cargo operations. It suits owner's condition checks, on-hire and off-hire records and pre-purchase work better than a full survey scope.

faqs.q: Do tankers at the refinery berths allow gauging of cargo tanks?
faqs.a: Not during cargo operations. Cargo tank entry needs a gas-free ship and a valid enclosed-space permit, which the terminal will not allow while the ship is loading or discharging. At the jetty we gauge the deck, piping and ballast spaces, and leave cargo tank work to a yard stay or a lay-up.

faqs.q: How does the steelworks' output affect scheduling?
faqs.a: Ore and coal calls follow the plant's production, so arrival dates can shift. We keep visa applications moving and fix flights only when the berth date is firm, which avoids wasted travel. If a ship waits at anchor longer than planned, the delay can be used for a condition survey of accessible spaces.
